bodyShopDispatch._doc: Body-Shop dispatch tunables (#314, parent #297). The Tier-3 mirror of serviceDispatch, fed into the SAME shared department-dispatch engine (advisor pick, parts gate, min(bays,advisors) capacity, read-model). Differs from Service in PRICING: there is no competitive↔premium dial — revenue is governed by the insurance/retail CHANNEL posture. Insurance (DRP) jobs are rate-capped (insuranceRateMultiplier ~1.0 — the insurer sets the rate; CollisionStream already capped the baseRevenue below book), retail (customer-pay) jobs are player-priced (lerp(retailFloorMultiplier, retailCeilMultiplier, posture)). bays start at Tier 3 (the Body Shop is dark below the showroom tier); collision jobs are slower + tolerate longer waits than Service tickets. All magnitudes placeholders pending the S14 calibration pass (#286).

motivatedSeller._doc: The per-listing multiplier on the engine's anchor that sets an auction asking price (#160). Retuned in the #286 calibration pass. The auction is the WHOLESALE market, and this module already states where wholesale sits relative to book: `inventory.wholesale.haircutPct` pays out book x 0.85 when you dump a unit. Centering the buy side at 1.0 contradicted that — you bought at book and could only sell back at 0.85, and a 1.20 ceiling let you pay 20% OVER book at a dealer auction. Centering at 0.85 makes the two sides of the same market symmetric: buy a unit and immediately dump it and you are roughly flat (less whatever recon you spent), which is the honest invariant. The dealer's margin now comes from buying right and retailing, not from a markup the customer pays.

valueHeatBands._doc: Display bands for the KPI dashboard used-value pressure readout (#179). segmentHeat is a signed fractional bookValue modifier; |heat| < mild reads AT BASELINE, mild..strong reads mildly above/below, >= strong reads strongly above/below. Presentation-only; calibration-neutral placeholders.

carrying._doc: Daily per-vehicle floorplan + carrying cost accrual (#173). Floorplan interest = currentBook × apr / 365; apr is the floorplan rate for the dealership's CareerProgression tier (better tier → cheaper money, a diegetic progression reward) and falls back to `baselineApr` for any tier without an explicit entry. `insurancePerDay`/`overheadPerDay` are flat per-unit-per-day allocations; `reconFadePerDay` is a small additive that only applies once recon is complete (a detailed car depreciating while it sits). A unit is visually flagged `aged` once `daysInInventory` exceeds `agedThresholdDays`. Retune the burn here without touching code.

wholesale._doc: The release valve on owned inventory (#362, A2 R2). Wholesaling a unit pays `currentBook × (1 − haircutPct)`, rounded, floored at 0 — the haircut is what a wholesale buyer takes for buying a car sight-unseen to resell, and it is why dumping a unit realizes a loss rather than being a free undo. Available for ANY owned unit regardless of recon progress or frontline hold: one rule, no second ceiling to learn. Magnitude is a placeholder pending the C2 calibration campaign (#286).

installedBase._doc: InstalledBase owner registry + return cadence (#298/#300, parent #297). `loyaltySeedScale` maps a deal's satisfaction-at-sale retentionSeed ∈ [0,1] onto an owner's initial loyalty. `returnCadence` is the service-due interval in game days per powertrain (EVs cycle least often). `jobCategoryDrift` walks early→late job categories as the car ages: each band applies while ageDays < untilAgeDays, the last (no untilAgeDays) is the catch-all. `returnRoll` carries the convenience/price-sensitivity terms of P(return) = clamp01(loyalty × reputation × convenience − priceSensitivity). All numbers are S14 (#286) calibration placeholders.

serviceInsights._doc: ServiceInsights read-model (#308, parent #297) — the trailing-window accumulator that backs the Service page demand-heat + base-health readouts. `demandWindowSize` is how many recent intake tickets the per-category heat is computed over; `heatThresholds` band a category's share×4 (1.0 = even split): at/above `hot` reads HOT, at/below `cold` reads COLD, else WARM. `demandTrendEpsilon` is the newer-vs-older-half share delta below which a category's demand trend reads steady. `baseHealthWindowDays` is the trailing day count the return/defection rates + trends average over; `baseTrendEpsilon` is the per-day count delta below which those trends read steady. All numbers are S14 (#286) calibration placeholders.

bodyShopInsights._doc: BodyShopInsights read-model (#315, parent #297) — the Tier-3 mirror of serviceInsights backing the Body Shop page demand-heat + conquest-health readouts. `demandWindowSize`/`heatThresholds`/`demandTrendEpsilon` band per-collision-category demand exactly like serviceInsights (share×4: at/above `hot` HOT, at/below `cold` COLD, else WARM; the newer-vs-older-half share delta below which a category trend reads steady). The conquest readout (Body Shop is conquest-dominant, no installed base): `conquestWindowDays` is the trailing day count the collision-flow volume rate + trend average over; `volumeTrendEpsilon` is the per-day intake-count delta below which the volume trend reads steady; `channelTrendEpsilon` is the newer-vs-older-half retail-share delta below which the channel-mix trend reads steady. All numbers are S14 (#286) calibration placeholders.

partsInventory._doc: PartsInventory par-level procurement (#301/#312, parent #297). `categories` carries each part category's `baseUnitCost` (the standard-tier unit price) plus its default `reorderPoint`/`target` par levels. The four Body-Shop categories (windows_glass / doors_panels / interior_trim / paint, #312) ship at 0 par — they are keyed so stock/consume/coverage work, but stay INACTIVE (no auto-order) until the Body-Shop package activates them with non-zero par at Tier 3, so a single shared parts room never auto-stocks collision parts before the body shop opens. `supplierTiers` trade unit cost against lead time and reliability: `costMultiplier` scales baseUnitCost, `leadTimeDays` is the scheduled arrival delay, `reliability` ∈ [0,1] is the per-order on-time probability (a failed seeded roll adds `delayPenaltyDays`). `defaultTier` is the tier a category procures at until the player picks another. All numbers are S14 (#286) calibration placeholders.

managerGates._doc: Channel-desk manager capability gates (#289+, docs/planning/manager-roles-channel-desk.md §3). Each acting capability earns a hard threshold on its own skill axis (0–100). M2 (#289) consumes pricing: top UCM pricing >= threshold unlocks the standing auto-pricing policy; below = suggestion-only. M3 (#290) consumes t_o_closing: top UCM t_o_closing >= threshold lets the UCM desk ALL below-floor discounts; below = the understaffed path (rare rate-gated escalation, the rest walk). M4 (#291) consumes condition_reading: top UCM condition_reading >= threshold lets the UCM auto-approve ALL escalated trades (the GM trumps this gate); below = the unusual trade escalates to the player. Appraisal advice (getTradeConditionRead) stays free on hire and is NOT gated here — only the act side. Placeholder magnitudes — calibrated in the S14 pass (#286). Green UCM ~50, seasoned ~72–82, so 60 sits each gate as an earned mid-career step.

executionDrift._doc: Execution-fidelity drift (M5 #292, docs/planning/manager-roles-channel-desk.md §4). Above an act gate the UCM aims at the player's setpoint; skill governs the gap (skill = fidelity + success). deficit = clamp01(1 - skill/skillReference); the drift fraction fills [0, deficit*maxDriftFraction) (signed two-sided for pricing mis-pricing, one-sided-worse for desking/trade), scaled by NPC.skillDriftFraction/signedSkillDrift and deterministic in (skill, seed). A green-but-gated UCM (~60) drifts noticeably; a seasoned one (skillReference ~90) holds tight. Placeholder magnitudes — calibrated in the S14 pass (#286).

serviceManager._doc: Service-manager automation gates (#310, parent #297). The Service-side mirror of the channel-desk gates: a later-tier service manager whose top `shop_throughput` skill clears a function's threshold takes over that standing Service decision. A LADDER (par lowest → capacity highest) so automation engages one function at a time as the SM grows; below a gate (or no SM) the player keeps manual control. Function tuning lives in data/service-manager.json. Placeholders pending the S14 calibration pass (#286).

bodyShopManager._doc: Body-shop-manager automation gates (#316, parent #297). The Tier-3 mirror of the serviceManager gates: a later-tier body-shop manager whose top `shop_throughput` skill clears a function's threshold takes over that standing Body-Shop decision. A LADDER (par lowest → capacity highest) so automation engages one function at a time as the manager grows; below a gate (or no manager) the player keeps manual control. NOTE: the Body Shop's marketing IS the insurance↔retail `channel` posture (the locked satellite table calls it 'channel choice — no separate mailer arms'), so the single `channel` rung is the unified pricing+marketing decision — there is no separate marketing gate. Function tuning lives in data/body-shop-manager.json. Placeholders pending the S14 calibration pass (#286).

tradePolicy._doc: Per-slot trade-acquisition policy (#172). The `multiplier` scales the staff's internal trade-in acceptance target (book × multiplier × read-confidence factor) inside DealEngine.evaluateTrade. Aggressive (>1) chases volume by paying over book — more trades acquired, thinner gross; Conservative (<1) protects gross by targeting under book — fewer trades, fatter margins; Market (1.0) appraises at honest book and is the default. The composition root resolves the selected id to its multiplier and threads it through the trade resolver; the setting persists per save slot. Retune the spread here without touching code.

policies.label: Aggressive
policies.blurb: Pay up to 10% over book to win trades — more cars acquired, thinner gross per deal.

policies.label: Market
policies.blurb: Appraise trades at honest book value — balanced acquisition rate and gross.

policies.label: Conservative
policies.blurb: Target ~8% under book to protect gross — fewer trades acquired, fatter margins.

fniPosture._doc: Per-slot F&I posture (#366) — the player's ONE finance-office input, and it is standing rather than per-deal (grill Q5/Q9/Q10: no slider, no per-product switch, no manual deal screen). `markupPts` is the rate markup in points of APR the desk works to, clamped down per deal to the credit tier's `markupCapPts`. Marking up harder earns more reserve on each contract AND raises the payment, so more buyers fail the PTI affordability gate that already exists — which is why 'More deals' is a real trade and not just a smaller number. The posture only bites once an f&i-manager is on the desk; with the desk empty the store earns `fniReserve.ambientMarkupPts` whatever is selected (grill Q2). The composition root resolves the selected id to its markup and hands DealEngine a live getter; the id persists on the save slot alongside tradePolicy/pricingStrategy/sourcingLean — no world-snapshot state (grill I7). Placeholder magnitudes owed to a #286-class calibration pass (grill I9). #373 adds `financedShareBand` — the share of a month's retail units that has to finance for THIS posture to have been the right standing bet, and the ONE rule behind the monthly F&I verdict on the Reveal. Reserve is earned on financed contracts only, so reaching for markup ('More per deal', floor 0.5) in a cash-paying month is a bet with nothing to bite on, and holding the rate down ('More deals', ceiling 0.8) in a month that financed nearly everything gives away gross the crowd would have paid. 'Balanced' spans the whole range because it is the posture that makes no bet on the mix — it can be beaten, never mismatched. The band judges the month that happened; it never feeds pricing.

postures.label: More per deal
postures.blurb: Mark the rate up as far as the lender allows — the most finance profit per contract, and the highest payment, so more buyers can't qualify.

postures.label: Balanced
postures.blurb: A normal market markup — solid finance profit without pricing many buyers out of their payment.

postures.label: More deals
postures.blurb: Keep the rate close to what the bank charges you — thin finance profit, but the lowest payment, so more buyers qualify.

fniDealKill._doc: Contractual deal-kill (#367) — the teeth that stop 'More per deal' from being strictly better than the other two postures (grill Q3 primary, I8). ONE curve, no per-lender branching: a contract written past the safe frontier of rate markup doesn't get bought — the lender passes on the paper, or the customer rate-shops it and leaves — so aggressive markup means fewer financed deals actually stick. `fallThroughRate = maxFallThroughRate x clamp01((markupPts - frontier) / fullKillRangePts)`, all in the same unit as `fniPosture.markupPts` and `credit-tiers.markupCapPts` (points of APR as decimals). At or under the frontier NOTHING falls through, which is why the Balanced posture and the unstaffed ambient markup both sit clean — and why a subprime buyer, whose lender caps markup at 0.0100, cannot be over-marked at all while a prime buyer can. This is the CONTRACTUAL kill; the structural one (a marked-up payment breaching ptiCap/maxTerm/ltvCeiling) already falls out of the existing affordability gate for free (grill I3) and is not re-implemented here. #369: the frontier is no longer flat — an F&I manager on the desk extends it with `finance_structuring`, `frontier = safeFrontierPts + structuringFrontierMaxPts x clamp01(skill / structuringSkillReference)`, which is Q5's 'the peak slides toward aggressive'. No desk ⇒ no extension ⇒ the bare `safeFrontierPts`, which is what leaves every pre-#369 calibration run byte-identical. The max extension is deliberately the distance from Balanced to 'More per deal' (0.0175 -> 0.0250): a structurer at the reference can run the aggressive posture with the lender never passing, and everything short of that reference is a real fall-through rate. Note it does NOT move `fniCsiDrag.fairMarkupPts` — a slicker structurer changes what the LENDER will buy, not how gouged the customer feels, so the aggressive posture never becomes free, it just changes which tooth bites. Placeholder magnitudes owed to a #286-class calibration pass (grill I9).

fniCsiDrag._doc: CSI drag (#368) — the second, SLOWER tooth on the F&I posture (grill Q3 secondary, I9). Deal-kill costs you the deal you were working; this costs you the next customer. A financed deal closed past `fairMarkupPts` publishes `reputation:satisfaction_hit`, and store satisfaction already feeds arrival rates, so gouging thins the crowd. `hit = maxSatisfactionHit x clamp01((markupPts - fairMarkupPts) / fullDragRangePts)`, flat past the end of the ramp for the same reason the kill curve is flat. The hit is on the MARKUP, never on the products — attaching a menu is the job, over-marking the rate is the gouge — so a cash deal has no drag at any attach. `fairMarkupPts` deliberately equals `fniDealKill.safeFrontierPts` today: both teeth measure how far past a fair markup the contract was written, so the player learns ONE frontier to read the dial rather than two. It is a separate key because the two are separately MEASURED (a probability against a satisfaction delta) and because #369 lets the F&I manager's `finance_structuring` move the lender's frontier — moving the customer's fairness line with it is a design decision, not a calibration nudge. Chargebacks are a later refinement layer on this same variable (Q3) and are not built here. Placeholder magnitudes owed to a #286-class calibration pass (grill I9): at the aggressive posture (0.0250) the excess is 0.0075 of a 0.0100 range, so a gouged close costs 0.75 x 1.5 = 1.13 satisfaction — against a walk's 0.12 charged ~2.6 times a day, i.e. a tooth that bites on the order of the walk drag rather than swamping it.

fniReserve._doc: Finance reserve (#365). The store sells the paper to the customer at `buyRate + markup` and the lender buys it at `buyRate`; the dealer's reserve is its share of the discounted spread over the loan's scheduled life. `dealerSharePct` is the lender's participation split (the lender keeps the rest). `ambientMarkupPts` is what a store with NO f&i-manager on the desk gets — the T1–T2 backend is ambient and minimal, with no player lever (grill Q2). A staffed desk works to the selected `fniPosture` markup instead; the desked target lives in that catalog and nowhere else (#366 deleted `balancedMarkupPts`, which was the same number in a second place). Both are clamped down to the credit tier's `markupCapPts`. Placeholder magnitudes owed to a #286-class calibration pass (grill I9).
